Math labels from R's plotmath notation

Source: R/plotmath.R
plotmath.Rd

plotmath() parses strings written in R's plotmath notation (see grDevices::plotmath) and returns tex() labels, the way ggplot2's parse = TRUE and label_parsed() parse theirs. tex() itself accepts the unparsed form: a call, a symbol or an expression, as made by quote(), bquote() or expression():

Usage

plotmath(text, display = FALSE)

Arguments

text

A character vector of plotmath strings. Each string is parsed with parse() and its first expression is used; an empty string gives an empty label.

display

As in tex().

Value

A vellum_tex_label (length-1 text) or a list of them.

Details

tex(quote(x[i]^2))
tex(expression(alpha + beta, sqrt(x, 3))) # a list of two labels
plotmath("hat(beta)[1] == 0.42")

The expression is translated to TeX (which becomes the label's source text, so queries, alt text and tooltips show the TeX) and typeset by the same engine.

Supported: x[i] and x^2; + - / * ~ (* juxtaposes, ~ adds a space); == != < > <= >=; !x; the %op% operators %+-% %/% %*% %.% %~~% %=~% %==% %prop% %~% %<->% %->% %<-% %up% %down% %<=>% %=>% %<=% %dblup% %dbldown% %subset% %subseteq% %supset% %supseteq% %notsubset% %in% %notin%; paste(), list(); sqrt(x) and sqrt(x, n); frac(), over(), atop(); hat() bar() tilde() dot() ring() widehat() widetilde() underline() phantom(); Greek letters by name (alpha, Omega, and plotmath's theta1 phi1 sigma1 omega1 Upsilon1); infinity partialdiff nabla degree minute second cdots ldots ... and aleph; sum() prod() integral() union() intersect() with optional lower and upper limits, and lim() min() max() inf() sup() with an optional lower one; group() and bgroup() (growing) delimiters, including lceil rceil lfloor rfloor langle rangle; italic() bold() plain() bolditalic(); displaystyle() textstyle() scriptstyle() scriptscriptstyle(); strings (set upright), numbers, (x) (drawn) and {x} (invisible grouping); and function calls such as f(x) or log(x).

One deliberate difference from base R graphics: single-letter symbols are set in math italic, the TeX convention, where base R sets them upright. Use plain() for upright letters. Longer names (mpg, Temperature) are set upright as one word, as in base R. Functions given the wrong number of arguments (frac(a)) are errors. Limits of sum(), integral(), lim() and friends go above and below the operator, as in base R. Anything else (symbol(), assignment, if, ...) is an error, not silently dropped.

See also

tex() for TeX notation, which covers more.

Examples

plotmath("alpha[i]^2 + beta")
#> <vellum::vellum_tex_label>
#>  @ tex    : chr "\\alpha_{i}^{2} + \\beta"
#>  @ display: logi FALSE
#>  @ text   : chr "\\alpha_{i}^{2} + \\beta"
plotmath(c("sqrt(x, 3)", "frac(1, n) * sum(x[i], i == 1, n)"))
#> [[1]]
#> <vellum::vellum_tex_label>
#>  @ tex    : chr "\\sqrt[3]{x}"
#>  @ display: logi FALSE
#>  @ text   : chr "\\sqrt[3]{x}"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> <vellum::vellum_tex_label>
#>  @ tex    : chr "\\frac{1}{n} \\sum\\limits_{i = 1}^{n} x_{i}"
#>  @ display: logi FALSE
#>  @ text   : chr "\\frac{1}{n} \\sum\\limits_{i = 1}^{n} x_{i}"
#> 
tex(quote(hat(mu) == bar(x)))
#> <vellum::vellum_tex_label>
#>  @ tex    : chr "\\hat{\\mu} = \\bar{x}"
#>  @ display: logi FALSE
#>  @ text   : chr "\\hat{\\mu} = \\bar{x}"
k <- 3
tex(bquote(x^.(k)))
#> <vellum::vellum_tex_label>
#>  @ tex    : chr "x^{3}"
#>  @ display: logi FALSE
#>  @ text   : chr "x^{3}"
